page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Recognise the log-derivative form
steps.margin_note: First mark. ∫f'(x)/f(x) dx = log|f(x)| — a formula worth recognising on sight.
steps.memory_tip: Whenever the numerator is the exact derivative of the denominator, the antiderivative is always a log.
steps.why: The numerator 2x is exactly the derivative of the denominator 1+x², so the integral is of the standard form ∫f'(x)/f(x) dx = log|f(x)|.
common_mistakes: Missing the derivative-of-denominator pattern and attempting an unnecessary substitution.
Writing the antiderivative without the modulus sign.

steps.label: Apply the limits and simplify
steps.margin_note: Second mark. log a − log b = log(a/b) — always combine before reporting the final value.
steps.memory_tip: 10/5 = 2, so the final answer is simply log2.
steps.why: Subtracting two logs is the same as taking the log of their quotient, so log10 − log5 collapses to log2 directly.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer as log10 − log5 instead of combining it.
